COMPLETE EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
————————————————  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) in an event-study framework (i.e., staggered, multi-event DiD).

Why it fits  
• Research question is causal (“does privileged information lead to … ?”).  
• We observe plausibly exogenous public‐information release dates (ratings downgrades, SEC 8-K restatements, Chapter-11 filings, large negative earnings surprises).  
• Any CDS trading that systematically occurs only for firms whose creditors already possessed the private information must appear in the days / weeks before the public release.  
• We can therefore compare the pre-event evolution of CDS spreads and market-quality outcomes for:  
 (a) firms whose creditor network makes them susceptible to insider trading (treated) versus  
 (b) firms whose creditors are unlikely to have material private information (control).  
• Because each firm can experience several events, we can include firm and calendar-date fixed effects, sharply purging time-invariant firm heterogeneity and market-wide shocks.

The same DiD setup, with a second-stage regression, will quantify whether any pre-event CDS informed trading harms (i) post-event bond spreads, (ii) equity returns, and (iii) equity/credit liquidity.

================================================================  
2. Treatment and Control  
————————————————  
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 if, at the event date, the reference entity has “high information‐access lenders.” Baseline definition: number of relationship banks (DealScan) in the top-15 global CDS dealers ≥ median (16). Alternative cut-offs: 75th percentile; a dummy for having at least one of the top-5 dealers.  
 Intuition: more such lenders ⇒ more probability that at least one desk trades on the inside information.

Control group  
Firms in the same CDS universe and period whose relationship‐bank count is below the chosen threshold.

Treatment timing / event date  
Day 0 = first public disclosure the market can legally trade on (ratings action, bankruptcy filing, 8-K, earnings release).  
Estimation window: [-60, +20] trading days.  
“Post” in DiD = [0,+20]; “Pre” = [-60,-1]. We will also estimate flexible leads/lags for an event-study graph.

Key outcomes  
• Abnormal CDS spread change (ΔCDS minus market-wide change).  
• CDS bid-ask spread.  
• Corporate bond yield spread.  
• Equity daily return and quoted spread/dollar depth (TAQ).

================================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
————————————————  
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of private-information trading, CDS spreads (and other outcomes) for high- and low-lender firms would evolve similarly in the pre-event window.  
 Plausibility: Same industry × rating × year fixed effects and firm fixed effects, plus evidence from visually flat pre-trends in the lead coefficients.

A2. No differential shock coinciding exactly with the upcoming public event that affects treated firms only through channels other than creditors’ private information.  
 Plausibility: We use firm fixed effects; events are idiosyncratic; will control for contemporaneous credit-market indices and macro surprises.

A3. Information release dates are not manipulable by the creditors (banks cannot time Moody’s downgrade).  
 Plausibility strong for ratings downgrades/bankruptcies; weaker for earnings releases ⇒ will run separate analyses for “hard” (downgrade/bankruptcy) vs. “soft” events.

================================================================  
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations  
————————————————  
T1. Confounding firm fundamentals  
 • Mitigation: Firm fixed effects; controls for daily equity return, option-implied vol, cash-flow news, bond index spreads.

T2. Anticipatory trading by non-relationship investors  
 • Mitigation: Compare only within CDS-quoted firms; include analyst coverage and news-wire counts interacted with time to show patterns are unique to treated group; placebo tests at pseudo-event dates.

T3. Treatment misclassification (banks with info lend to some “control” firms)  
 • Mitigation: Use alternative, continuous treatment (log # informed lenders); instrument for lender information intensity using past bank mergers that mechanically added an informed lender to some borrowers (first-stage F > 10 expected).

================================================================  
5. R Code Outline (executable)  
————————————————  

```r
# 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)    # fast data manipulation
library(fixest)        # fast high-dim FE regressions
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data loading ----------------------------------------------------------
cds   <- fread("cds_quotes.csv")          # firm, date, bid, ask
equ   <- fread("crsp_daily.csv")          # firm, date, ret, volume
bond  <- fread("corp_bond_spreads.csv")   # firm, date, oas
rel   <- fread("bank_relationships.csv")  # firm, year, n_rel_banks
events<- fread("credit_events.csv")       # firm, event_date, event_type

# 2. Merge & variable construction ----------------------------------------
cds[, mid := 0.5*(bid+ask)]
setkey(cds, firm, date)
setkey(equ,  firm, date)
setkey(bond, firm, date)

panel <- Reduce(function(x,y) merge(x,y, all=TRUE, by=c("firm","date")),
                list(cds[,.(firm, date, mid, bid, ask)],
                     equ[,.(firm, date, ret)],
                     bond))
panel[, ym := year(date)*100 + month(date)]

# Add treatment intensity (time-varying by calendar year)
rel[, ym := year(event_date)*100 + month(event_date)]
panel <- merge(panel, rel[,.(firm, ym, n_rel_banks)], 
               by=c("firm","ym"), all.x=TRUE)
panel[, treated := as.integer(n_rel_banks >= median(n_rel_banks, na.rm=TRUE))]

# Attach event timing ------------------------------------------------------
events[, `:=`(t0 = as.IDate(event_date))]
panel <- merge(panel, events[,.(firm, t0)], by="firm", all.x=TRUE)

panel[, rel_day := as.numeric(date - t0)]             # e.g., -60…+20
panel <- panel[rel_day >= -60 & rel_day <= 20]

# Outcome variables
panel[, d_cds := mid - shift(mid, 1, type="lag"), by=firm]
panel[, bid_ask := ask - bid]

# 3. Main DiD regression ---------------------------------------------------
spec_main <- feols(d_cds ~ treated*I(rel_day>=0) | firm + date, 
                   data = panel[!is.na(d_cds) & rel_day %between% c(-60,20)],
                   cluster = ~firm)

summary(spec_main)

# 4. Event-study coefficients (plot) ---------------------------------------
panel[, post_bin := factor(rel_day)]
evst <- feols(d_cds ~ i(post_bin, treated, ref=-1) | firm + date,
              data=panel, cluster=~firm)
iplot(evst)

# 5. Robustness: placebo pseudo-events -------------------------------------
set.seed(123)
pseudo <- events[,.(firm, t0 = sample(date,1)), by=firm]  # uniform draw
panel_p <- merge(panel[, !'t0'], pseudo, by="firm")
panel_p[, rel_day := as.numeric(date - t0)]
placebo <- feols(d_cds ~ treated*I(rel_day>=0) | firm + date,
                 data = panel_p[rel_day %between% c(-60,20)],
                 cluster=~firm)
summary(placebo)
```

================================================================  
6. Expected Results  
————————————————  
• CDS mid quotes for treated firms should begin to widen relative to control starting 10-20 trading days before the public event.  
• Magnitude: For an average downgrade that ultimately increases CDS by 80 bps, I expect ~15–25 bps of that widening to occur early for treated firms.  
• Post-event, treated firms’ bonds and equities should display larger one-day price drops and wider bid-ask spreads, consistent with liquidity deterioration because insiders already incorporated part of the information.

================================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)  
————————————————  
C1: No differential pre-trends ➔ 1 (will test graphically)  
C2: Treatment cannot affect control’s outcomes ➔ 1  
C3: No simultaneous shocks differing by treatment ➔ 0.5 (earnings events still risky)  
C4: Stable composition (no sample attrition correlated with treatment) ➔ 1  
C5: SUTVA satisfied (insider trading in one firm does not move another’s CDS materially) ➔ 0.5  

Overall = 4/5: credible but still needs careful robustness work.
